findings.reason: §16 argues at length that the core layer should own the normaliser, so it must name the existing schema predicate and say whether it stays a predicate distinct from the derivation or is folded under the same owner.
findings.text: the plan reworks the section-identity vocabulary and hoists section_record_id and section_id_candidates into the core layer but never cites the existing is_section_identity in _schema.py, the one symbol that already owns "is this a usable section identity", so a reader meets three identity names and a predicate whose relationship the plan does not state

findings.reason: the plan should extend section_record_id to accept the enclosing element's attributes (or make the adapter private) instead of adding a third public identity symbol beside the normaliser it is hoisting.
findings.text: the plan hoists section_record_id (the canonical identity derivation) into reckon/_plan_html.py and in the same change adds a second public derivation, section_identity, over two attribute mappings, so one module ends up owning section identity twice; the two-mapping signature is the only difference and could be a parameter of section_record_id rather than a parallel name

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 consolidates nine store helpers and the wrapper-id resolution onto one parser, and §16/§18 relocate rather than spread machinery; the interfaces added are smaller than the behaviour they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 adds a new public section_identity beside the section_record_id it hoists into the same module, so section identity derivation has two owners where one is being extended.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; each of §16 (section_identity), §17 (plan_headings) and §18 (hoisted reader) names its one added public definition and names what it retires or moves (section_record_id/section_id_candidates hoisted, landed_section_ids moved, the private promotion reader retired) or states why nothing is retired, so no section adds surface unaccounted.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched the named codebase and cites section_record_id, section_id_candidates, _StructuredSectionSpanParser, list_plan_reviews, promotion._plan_remaining_sections and doccheck._implementable_section_ids, but omits the existing third symbol of the same vocabulary, reckon/_schema.py:is_section_identity.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one genuinely thin layer, §16's coverage predicate, is joined over two existing readers (outstanding sections × stored section digests) rather than forwarding, and the plan states its consumers.
